Grandpa Wendell’s Catnip Mouse

“It’s for Pom-Pom. She deserves nice things.”

Read this aloud

Grandpa Wendell comes home from the pet shop with a paper bag, and through the paper you can smell it: catnip. A whole catnip mouse, red felt, with a string tail. His daughter June is in the kitchen putting the kettle on. In the front window, a large fluffy grey cat called Pom-Pom watches you all with deep contempt.

House Standard · Patience 9 · The prize catnip mouse (Small) · Gone at the start of round 9 · Den Bathroom

Who lives here Grandpa Wendell, June, Pom-Pom, The robot vacuum

For four cats. With three: Patience 10, gone at the start of round 11, Lights Out at the end of round 13, 3 Cattitude each. With five: Patience 8. The Robbery Tracker does this for you.

Grandpa Wendell’s house has a hall, a front room where Pom-Pom rules, a kitchen with Pom-Pom’s microchip cat flap, a cellar under the kitchen with a cracked window, and upstairs a spare bedroom, a landing and the bathroom. The mouse is small — one cat can carry it — but it has to get out of the house, and Pom-Pom will want it too.

How it plays

  • Grab the mouse from the paper bag in the hall before Grandpa gives it to Pom-Pom at the start of round 4. After that you have to get past her.
  • Grandpa dozes. A sleeping Grandpa sees nothing — perfect for a quick snatch.
  • The robot vacuum tempts Hunters wherever it goes — and can be ridden.
  • Getting out is the hard part: plan the exit before you grab the mouse.

The Prize Clock

WhenThe prize
Start of round 1Grandpa Wendell puts it in the hall and stays there this round. Step 1: Streetwise or Sneaky, Tricky.
Start of round 4Grandpa Wendell puts it in the living room and stays there this round. No roll to get at it.
Start of round 9Gone — if the gang isn't holding it.
End of round 11Lights Out: any cat still inside is pinched.

The rooms

RoomTemptsNotes
HallCuriousFront door (behind Grandpa): big, Sneaky, Hard; or Sweet, round 1 only
Living roomHunter, Lap Cat, Box Sitter—
KitchenFoodie, Knockerdoor to the cellar (Streetwise, Tricky; or Savage, Hard); Pom-Pom's microchip cat flap (jam it open): normal, Streetwise, Tricky, noisy
CellarHunter, Curiousdoor to the kitchen (Streetwise, Tricky; or Savage, Hard); Cracked cellar window: tight, no roll
Landing——
Spare bedroomClimber, Box SitterSpare bedroom window (up the drainpipe): normal, a climb (Small things only), Sneaky or Savage, Hard
BathroomBox Sitterthe Den

Ways: Hall–Living room (big), Hall–Kitchen (big), Kitchen–Cellar (normal), Hall–Landing (normal), Landing–Spare bedroom (big), Landing–Bathroom (big).

Pom-Pom’s cat flap only opens for her microchip; jam it (Streetwise, Tricky) and it stays open for everyone — but it rattles every time a cat goes through (a noisy entrance). The front door lets one cat in behind Grandpa in round 1. The cellar window is Tight: Lean cats only. The bedroom window is up the drainpipe: Hard.

Who lives here

Grandpa Wendell (Grandparent)

Attention 0 · starts in the hall. Routine (d6): 1–2 stays put; 3–4 Hall; 5 Living room; 6 Kitchen.

Dozes: every house's turn, on a 1–2 on an extra d6, falls asleep until the end of the next round; only a Prize Clock job wakes them.

June (Grown-up)

Attention 1 · starts in the kitchen. Routine (d6): 1–3 stays put; 4 Living room; 5 Hall; 6 Landing.

Pom-Pom (House cat)

Rating 2 · guards the living room. Soft: Sweet can befriend her.

The robot vacuum (Robot vacuum)

Starts in the living room; wanders Living room, Hall, Kitchen. Tempts Hunters; can be ridden.

The getaway

  1. The garden wall — Savage or Sneaky.
  2. The greenhouse — Sneaky or Streetwise, Tricky.
  3. The canal fence — Savage or Sneaky, Tricky. The Canal Street Toms hang about here, and nick any loot that's dropped.
  4. The footbridge — Savage or Sneaky.

Then the hideout. The loot is 1 piece.

Cred (Chapter 9): the catnip stash is Grandpa’s pots of catnip on the windowsill (spare bedroom). The Canal Street Toms have tagged the cellar.

Running Grandpa Wendell's Catnip Mouse in Foundry

  1. Open the Robbery Tracker (the cat button on the token controls) and choose Start a robbery: pick this house and the gang. Every cat starts outside, with its starting Cattitude.
  2. Begin round runs the Prize Clock and, if anyone can be tempted, whispers you one-click Tempt buttons.
  3. Players move and act from the tracker (or roll from their cat sheets). The roll dialog fills in the Knack, help, Difficulty, the pet and who is watching; the card offers Push and Accept, and you can flip Seen.
  4. End round rolls the house's turn in the open: pets, noise, routines and Searching, holders, then Finding it.
  5. The house part ends at Lights Out, or at the end of a round when no free cat is left inside and the prize is out, eaten or gone (or when you press End the robbery because the gang runs for it). Any cat still inside is pinched.
  6. The getaway follows in the same tracker: the loot is shared out, each cat rolls over the next obstacle (help a friend and go over together; a Flop drops loot), and End the getaway round brings the warden on and corners the stragglers, who dodge or go in the van. When everyone is home or pinched, the loot is counted and the outcome is posted.
  7. Cred scores itself: any cat can Tag its room (one tag a room for the gang), the catnip stash tempts every cat in its room (or a cat gets into it on purpose) and gives that cat the zoomies, and the rivals wait on the getaway. The tracker keeps each cat's Cred (with − and + for you), and the outcome card names the Cat's Whiskers.

Every automation can be switched off in the system settings. The residents of this house are in the Residents compendium; the tracker works without them.
